notes:
v0.6.40: fix two more launch-day bugs on a fresh build.

1. Modem73 Interface: Start silently failed.
   Root cause: start_modem73_loopback.sh used `&` + `disown`
   to background modem73. When the script's parent (the launcher
   route's Popen) exited with `exit 0`, the script's session
   (start_new_session=True) got SIGHUP'd by the kernel. The
   backgrounded modem73 — disowned but not nohup'd — died ~2s
   later. The HTTP 302 came back fine, but modem73 was never
   actually running.

   Fix: use `nohup modem73 ... &` in start_modem73_loopback.sh.
   nohup tells the kernel "ignore SIGHUP" for that process, so
   the session-leader's exit doesn't kill it. Same fix applied
   to start_pavucontrol.sh which had the same `disown` pattern.
   (start_fldigi / start_flrig / start_js8call / start_wsjtx /
   start_patmenu / start_freedata already used nohup and worked
   correctly; this was an audit miss.)

2. Wifi button + app help links in the launcher 404'd.
   Root cause: the bootstrap never installed node-portal.
   g90-image/node-portal/app.py + templates/ existed in the
   repo, but the bootstrap had no install step. The Wifi button
   pointed to :8081/wifi.html, which doesn't exist as a route
   in node-portal (the wifi scan is at /scan; the index page at
   / has the scan button).

   Fix:
   - Bootstrap now installs /home/pi/node-portal/ with app.py
     and templates, creates /usr/local/bin/start-node-portal
     wrapper, and adds /etc/systemd/system/node-portal.service.
   - Bootstrap enables + starts node-portal.service.
   - app.py updated to read PORT from env (default 8081).
     The old code hardcoded port=8090, which made the wrapper
     irrelevant and clashed with the launcher's default port.
   - Launcher template: Wifi link :8081/wifi.html → :8081/
     (the index page that has the scan button).

Effect: fresh-flash reticulumpi now has node-portal running
on :8081, matching g90digi. The Wifi button + every app help
link (FLrig, JS8Call, FLDigi, WSJT-X) on the launcher all
work. The Modem73 Interface: Start button actually keeps
modem73 running.
